newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canon profits hit record high on PC boom, weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Canon profits hit record high on PC boom, weak yen.

text.p: Canon Inc, a top manufacturer of cameras, printers and photocopiers, said on Wednesday it earned record profits in 1996, drawing strength from the global boom in personal computers and the weaker yen.
The company expected the good news to continue this year, forecasting that healthy sales of computer printers would help propel group net profits to the 100 billion yen mark ($806 million) in 1997.
"Computer peripherals such as bubble-jet printers and laser printers will remain brisk, helping push up sales," a Canon director told reporters.

Canon on Wednesday announced 1996 group net profits of 94.2 billion yen ($759 million), up a dramatic 71 percent from the year before and above the previous record of 61.4 billion yen ($495 million) in 1990.

Group sales also set a new record in 1996 for the third year in a row, rising 18 percent to 2.56 trillion yen ($20.6 billion), with a further increase to 2.78 trillion yen ($22.4 billion) projected for this year.
The company said last year's introduction of new bubble-jet models boosted sales of printers for home-use, while office-use laser printers also enjoyed brisk sales.

Buoyed by a worldwide personal computer boom, revenues in Canon's office equipment division rose 17.4 percent in 1996 to 2.1 trillion yen ($16.9 billion), or more than 80 percent of total group sales.
The weaker yen also helped buoy Canon's earnings last year by increasing revenues from exports.
"The weaker yen rate raised our pre-tax profit estimate for this year by 16 billion yen ($129 million)," he said.

Canon president Fujio Mitarai told Reuters in an interview on Friday that his company should be able to expand its group sales to four trillion yen ($32.2 billion) in calendar 2000 if the yen does not surge back to around 110 yen to the dollar.
He also said Canon aims to become the global market leader among printer manufacturers.
At present, Hewlett-Packard Co of the United States holds about half of the world's ink-jet printer market, followed by Canon's 30 percent, analysts said.

Canon's group earnings announcement came after the Tokyo stock market was closed. Canon shares ended down 50 yen at 2,660 yen on active profit taking after rallying to a lifetime high of 2,820 yen last Thursday.
The results followed last week's announcement of record profits for the parent company in 1996 of 125.23 billion yen ($1.00 billion), up 56 percent.
Canon's solid performance has already made it a favourite among global investors, who have been buying up shares of Japan's so-called "Nifty Fifty" blue chip companies. ($1=124 yen)
